key_insight: Citizen-led PV systems stay economically viable under falling solar-era electricity prices mainly through collective coordination and flexible energy-sharing rules, not just through more technology.
engineering_relevance: For distributed PV design, the main optimization target shifts from maximizing surplus export to improving self-consumption, allocation fairness, and governance under real market constraints.
method: Analyzed high-resolution consumption data from a rural community with 24 users sharing one PV facility.
Compared static, dynamic, and hybrid energy-sharing schemes, with and without battery storage.
Evaluated impacts on PV capacity needs, investment cost, annual savings, and benefit distribution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that collective self-consumption lowered required PV capacity and costs, while battery storage added limited value except under specific market conditions.
watch_item: Fairer allocation and hybrid governance can improve participation, but they add operational complexity and their benefits depend on local price and remuneration rules.
paper_title: Decision-support strategies for photovoltaic self-consumption under declining electricity prices and limited remuneration of surplus generation
